newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ends Burma's trade privileges over forced labour.
newsitem.headline: EU ends Burma's trade privileges over forced labour.

text.p: The European Union stripped Burma of special trading privileges on Monday because of reports that it uses forced labour to boost exports.
The decision was taken by the General Affairs Council, following advice from the European Commission which investigated the allegations by non-governmental groups.

The Commission said Burma failed to cooperate with the investigation. Under the decision, it will no longer be eligible for so-called Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) trade benefits on agricultural and industrial products.
In a statement released in Brussels, Human Rights Watch welcomed the decision, calling it an unprecedented step by the EU.
It said it testified at hearings held by the European Commission in March and September 1996 in support of a complaint filed by international workers' organisations.

"We estimate that between 1992 and 1995 some two million civilians have been forced to work with no pay, often in appalling conditions and sometimes at gunpoint, to build up Burma's infrastructure and help attract foreign investment and tourism," it said.
EU-Burma trade totals around 41 million European currency units ($47.2 million) a year. About a quarter of that is subject to lucrative GSP trade breaks.
